long_term_demand.rationale: Official MIIT evidence shows combination-driving-assistance penetration in new Chinese passenger vehicles reached 70% in 2026 and a mandatory national safety standard for such systems has been issued for 2027 implementation. Bethel's official filings and production evidence show WCBS and EMB are execution-layer braking products for higher-level intelligent driving, with WCBS in large-scale delivery and EMB already moving from validation into mass production. The demand driver is therefore tied to a verified structural increase in assisted-driving and intelligent-chassis adoption rather than a single transient model cycle.

moat.rationale: Primary evidence shows a multi-year commercialization barrier rather than a prototype-only claim: Bethel spent six years developing EMB, built a validation stack exceeding 15,000 test cases, 2,000 validation prototypes and four million road-test kilometers, obtained ASIL-D functional-safety certification, passed 10,000 cumulative EMB units in 2026, and built an automated line planned for 1.2 million units per year. By September 2026 it had four OEM mass-production programs with expected lifetime sales above USD 300m. Together with existing large-scale WCBS delivery, this combination of safety certification, validation depth, embedded OEM programs and scaled manufacturing constitutes a verified replication barrier in brake-by-wire.

predictability.rationale: The audited 2025 annual report supplies three consecutive complete fiscal years (2023-2025) in one official table. Revenue rose from CNY 7.474bn to 9.937bn to 12.014bn; attributable net profit rose from CNY 0.891bn to 1.209bn to 1.309bn; operating cash flow stayed positive at CNY 0.678bn, 1.058bn and 0.867bn. Revenue and profit never breached the system's downside stability floors, cash-flow decline in 2025 was about 18% and remained well inside the -50% floor, and three-year profit/cash-flow volatility stayed far below the 5x ceiling. This meets the frozen strict multi-year accounting-predictability rule for a non-resource automotive-parts business.
